---

---

## 2. Trend structure: a completed breakdown, not a pullback

**The dominant fact: COIN is in a deeply established, multi-timeframe downtrend, and the 2026-11-23 session is the first meaningful counter-move.**

- **The decline.** COIN printed its window-high intraday at **208.33 on 2026-09-21** (peak close 201.07 on 2026-09-22). From that close to today's 108.78 is **−45.9%**. The final leg was violent: 127.65 (11-13) → 101.97 (11-20) = **−20.1% in five sessions**.
- **Structural range break.** The May–October trading range floor was ≈136.89–139.18 (intraday lows on 2026-10-30, 2026-07-31, 2026-06-26). COIN's **2026-11-20 low of 101.71 broke ~35 points below that six-month floor** — the lowest price in the entire available dataset. This is a genuine structural break, not a test of existing support; there is no historical shelf beneath 101.71 within this data window.
- **Event gap.** 2026-10-30 gapped from 160.59 (10-29 close) to an open of 148.23 and closed 143.54 — **−10.6% on 20,894,000 shares, the largest volume in the window**. (I have no news/calendar tool; the size and single-day character are consistent with a scheduled event, but that is inference, not confirmed data.) Every subsequent rally has failed below that gap.
- **Fully inverted moving-average stack.** Price sits below the 10 EMA (−7.8%), 20 SMA (−18.3%), 50 SMA (−32.8%) and 200 SMA (−36.8%), and the averages are stacked in perfect bearish order (10 < 20 < 50 < 200).
- **Confirmed loss of trend benchmarks (precise dates from the data):**
  - **200 SMA lost on 2026-10-07** (close 178.45 vs 200 SMA 184.49; it closed above 185.74 on 2026-10-06). No close above since.
  - **50 SMA lost on 2026-10-16** (close 173.16 vs 177.63), after a one-day failed reclaim on 2026-10-15 (183.81 vs 177.08). No close above since.
  - The **50 SMA is below the 200 SMA throughout the available window** (162.14 vs 172.17 today; 169.75 vs 187.80 on 2026-09-24) — a death-cross configuration that predates this data window, so I cannot date the cross itself.

---

## 3. Indicator-by-indicator read

### Momentum — RSI: deeply oversold, and that oversold condition is *being re-earned*
RSI(14) = **29.80**, up from **22.94 on 2026-11-20** (the lowest reading in the series). Sequence: 32.43 (11-13) → 29.23 → 27.44 → 25.84 → 25.26 → 22.94 → 29.80.
- **Critical nuance — there is no bullish divergence.** The prior oversold print on 2026-11-02 (RSI 29.70, close 137.83) versus 2026-11-20 (RSI 22.94, close 101.97) shows **lower price AND lower RSI**. Momentum is confirming, not diverging. Anyone calling a reversal off "RSI divergence" is not supported by this data.
- **The failure precedent matters.** After the 11-02 oversold print, RSI snapped to 40.65 by 2026-11-04 (close 151.50) — a **+9.9% two-day bounce — which then failed completely** and rolled to new lows. That is exactly the shape today's +6.7% bounce resembles, and it is the single strongest argument against chasing it.
- RSI has been below 35 almost continuously since 2026-11-05. In strong downtrends RSI stays pinned in the 20–35 band; it is a *trend* signal here, not an automatic reversal signal.

### MACD — still deteriorating; only a first-order pause
- MACD line **−15.85 vs signal −13.79** → line remains **below signal (no crossover)**. The line has fallen relentlessly from −4.36 (2026-10-26) to −15.85, an extreme reading.
- Histogram: −1.86 (11-16) → −2.14 → −2.38 → −2.41 → **−2.62 (11-20, the trough)** → −2.06 (11-23). The histogram improved on today's session only. **One improving histogram bar is a deceleration signal, not a trend-change signal** — note that the histogram also improved on 2026-11-11/11-12 (−1.86/−1.69) and the downtrend resumed immediately.
- MACD is far below zero, so any cross back above signal would initially be a "bear-market rally" signal, not a buy-and-hold signal.

### Volatility / mean-reversion — Bollinger: riding the lower band, not cleanly breaking it
- Bandwidth is **72.53 points = 54.5% of the 20 SMA (133.09)** — an extremely expanded band, itself evidence of a mature volatility regime.
- The lower band is falling fast: 118.68 (11-13) → 114.69 → 110.66 → 107.49 → 104.01 → 99.41 → **96.82 (11-23)**. Price hugs it rather than snapping back: closes on 11-16 through 11-20 sat *just above* the lower band each day (119.84 vs 114.69; 115.02 vs 110.66; 110.51 vs 107.49; 108.87 vs 104.01; 101.97 vs 99.41). This "band walk" is a classic persistent-distribution pattern and is **not** the profile of a V-bottom.
- The one genuine band break was the **2026-10-30 close of 143.54 versus a 149.81 lower band** — and that produced further downside, not a bounce. Today's close of 108.78 sits **11.96 points (12.4%) above the 96.82 lower band**, so a good deal of the mechanical "oversold" credit has already been consumed by today's rebound.

### Risk — ATR: stops and size must respect ~8% daily ranges
- ATR = **9.07** (8.34% of the 108.78 close), down from 11.36 (2026-10-05) and 10.82 (2026-11-06) — volatility is *contracting from an extreme*, which typically precedes either a compression break or a dead-cat reflex.
- Practical implication: a **2×ATR one-day envelope from today's close is roughly 90.6–126.9**. Any stop tighter than ~1 ATR (9 points) inside this regime will be hit by noise.

### Volume — the one genuinely constructive data point
- 10-day average volume ≈ **9.06M**; 20-day average ≈ **9.43M**. Today's 10,764,119 is **~14–19% above those averages on an up day** — supportive of real dip-buying.
- But: **2026-11-20's decline came on 14,096,400 shares**, heavier than today's rebound. The capitulation day still outweighs the bounce day on volume, so this is *not yet* a confirmed reversal volume signature.
- Session shape caveat: 11-23 gapped open at 109.56 and **closed at 108.78, below its own open**, having faded from the 111.40 high. The buyers were absorbed intra-session.

### Moving averages — overhead supply is layered and dense
10 EMA 117.94 → 20 SMA 133.09 → 50 SMA 162.14 → 200 SMA 172.17. Each is a distinct band of trapped supply. Notably, the **50/200 gap is narrowing** (18.05 points on 2026-09-24 → 10.03 today) purely because the 200 SMA is declining toward price — that is *not* a bullish development, it simply means the long-term average is still catching up to a large leg down.

---

## 4. Regime verdict and the central tension

**Regime: bearish continuation with a reflexive, oversold bounce in progress.**

The tension to trade around:
- **Bull case:** RSI trough (22.94) + MACD histogram trough (−2.62) + ATR contraction + above-average volume on the +6.7% day + a close 12.4% above the falling lower band = the *ingredients* of an oversold thrust.
- **Bear case (heavier):** every average above, MACD still below signal, **no RSI divergence**, a precedent for exactly this bounce failing (11-02 → 11-04 → new lows), the rebound closing below its own open, the capitulation day out-volume-ing the bounce day, and price 24 points below the lowest close of the prior six months with **no structural support between ~101.71 and the 96.82 band** — i.e., a vacuum below.

**Base probability assignment (judgment, not data):** a trend resumption to new lows before any durable base is built is more likely than a sustained reversal. Confirmation requires (a) a close above the 10 EMA at 117.94, (b) a MACD-line-over-signal cross, and (c) a higher low versus 101.71. As of today, **none of the three is satisfied.**

---

## 5. Actionable levels (all anchored to verified data)

| Resistance 1 | **111.40** | 2026-11-23 session high — today's fade point |

| Support 4 | **~92.7 / ~87.6** | Mechanical: 101.71 − 1×ATR / 101.71 − 1.5×ATR (projection, not historical level) |

---

## 6. Trade plans

**A. Short / hedge / stay-flat bias (aligned with the trend) — preferred**
- Enter on a failed rally into **117.94–122.99** (10 EMA plus the 11-16 shelf), requiring a rejection candle.
- Stop: **above 125.5** (beyond the 11-13 low / supply band). Risk ≈ 6–8 points.
- Targets: **T1 101.71** (retest of the dataset floor), **T2 96.82** (lower band), **T3 92.7** (1 ATR extension). R:R ≈ 1.5:1 to 2.5:1.
- Do **not** initiate a fresh short off today's 108.78 with RSI at 29.8 — that is selling into the only oversold condition present.

**B. Counter-trend long (aggressive, small size only)**
- Valid **only** above **111.40** on a close, and preferably only after a **close above 117.94 (10 EMA)** with a MACD/signal cross.
- Stop: **96.8–97.2** (0.5×ATR buffer below 101.71, confluencing exactly with the lower band at 96.82).
- Targets: **T1 125.38**, **T2 133.09 (20 SMA)**, **T3 136.89–148.23 gap**. R:R from 118 ≈ 1.3:1 / 2.5:1 / 3.8:1.
- If entering *unconfirmed* now (108.78) to front-run an oversold thrust, treat it as a **1–3 day scalp, half of normal size**, invalidation on any close below 101.97, first exit at 117.9–119.8. The 11-02→11-04 failure is the cautionary template.

**C. Base / swing case — no new exposure**
- A high-probability long setup only forms after a **higher low above 101.71** plus a reclaim of the 10 EMA, or after a full close back above the **2026-10-30 gap upper edge near 148.23**. Until then, COIN is a sell-the-rips market.

**Position sizing (mandatory at ATR 9.07 / 8.34%):** size so that a **1.5×ATR adverse move (≈13.6 points, ≈12.5%)** stays within your per-position risk budget. That is roughly **⅓ to ½ of the notional you would use in a normal-volatility name**. Options traders: realized/implied vol is extreme — short-premium strategies on this bounce carry tail risk of a violent squeeze.

---

## 7. What would change my mind (watch-list triggers)
1. **RSI > 40 with a higher low** — would mark the first genuine momentum repair.
2. **MACD line crossing above signal** while the histogram turns positive — first real momentum inflection.
3. **A close above 117.94 (10 EMA) on volume > 13M** — the first trend-filter breach by buyers.
4. **A close above 133.09 (20 SMA)** — would signal the band-walk regime has ended; this, not the 10 EMA, is the true regime flip.
5. **A close below 101.97** — confirms the breakdown continues into a support vacuum toward 96.82 and below.
6. **ATR expanding back above 11** — would mean a fresh volatility impulse, typically downward given the trend.

## COIN Sentiment Report — 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-23

### Source-by-source breakdown

#### Yahoo Finance news headlines: unavailable
Yahoo Finance news returned **DATA_UNAVAILABLE** after a failed vendor request. This means the institutional / fact-driven narrative for **COIN** could not be measured for the period. The absence of news is a data-quality gap, not a bearish or bullish signal about Coinbase Global, Inc. itself.

Because the news feed is unavailable, the analysis cannot compare headline framing against retail positioning, nor confirm whether any earnings, crypto-market, regulatory, product, or company-specific events occurred during the lookback window.

#### Reddit discussion: unavailable
Reddit feeds for **r/wallstreetbets**, **r/stocks**, and **r/investing** failed to fetch. No substantive longer-term community narrative could be assessed. This is another major gap: Reddit would typically help identify whether **COIN** discussion is dominated by trade speculation, fundamental crypto exposure, earnings expectations, regulatory narratives, or broader market sentiment.

The unavailable Reddit data should not be interpreted as a lack of discussion.

#### StockTwits messages: only usable source
StockTwits is the only source with data. The screening note says 19 of 30 fetched posts are about **COIN**, with a classifier stance split of **7 bullish, 8 bearish, 1 neutral, 3 unclear**. The user-tagged label counts in the displayed sample are **5 bullish, 8 bearish, 6 unlabeled** out of 19 messages. Both views point to a roughly split retail tape with a modest bearish edge in explicit user tags, though the classifier’s on-topic stance count is closer to balanced.

**Bullish signals**
- Several users expressed directional conviction tied to Coinbase’s crypto exposure: “Once btc start going up, it will be in the range between 180 and 200!!”
- One user posted a promotional-style call-options setup with a **$108.82** underlying price, Dec 18, 2026 $110 calls, buy zone $6.67–$8.24, target zone $12.10–$14.79, and “Potential Upside: 71% ROI.” This is not high-quality sentiment on its own, but it indicates active speculative interest in upside exposure.
- Bullish short-term price targets included “strong buy! Chart shows $120 incoming,” “Very bullish, next rally incoming!,” and long-term speculation such as “500 in 2027.”
- Some bearish-sounding posts are partly conditional: “wait until the 80’s if you rlly wanna buy” implies the market is viewed as a trading vehicle rather than a failed business.

**Bearish signals**
- Explicit downside calls clustered around a failure of the $100 level: “under 100 tomorrow!” and “ALLLLLLLLLL TIMEEEEEEEEEEE LOWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW INCOMING.”
- A volume/credibility complaint stated: “piss poor volume despite up in price. It’s all algo trading. No one give a flying fk about this POS stock. Crypto is dead.” This is meaningful as a bearish retail narrative: the move in **COIN** was not viewed as conviction-driven by at least one participant.
- Regulatory/political disappointment appeared in the note that it would be better if the Clarity Act advanced before political turnover, suggesting sentiment is linked to crypto-policy expectations rather than only company fundamentals.
- One post referenced Bitcoin skepticism: “at least we aren’t fading too largely with this scam pump and dump on bitcoin today,” implying the broader crypto proxy may be vulnerable.

**Neutral / ambiguous signals**
- An options-flow message described a large May 2027 call order, about **$463K**, and broader premium around **$26.8M** across approximately **73,000 contracts**, but labeled the overall options split as close to evenly distributed and “neutral.” That supports active derivatives speculation but does not provide a clear directional signal.
- “hold that line lol” and “111 is where Fridays ass raping began as well. Clear resistance” identify price levels but do not state conviction. The repeated focus on roughly **$110–$111** as resistance is important.

### Cross-source divergences and alignment
The most important divergence is not between bullish and bearish traders, but between **available data and unavailable context**. StockTwits is the only observable sentiment layer, and it is internally split. News and Reddit are unavailable, so there is no institutional confirmation or contradiction of the retail read.

Within StockTwits, there is a mild divergence between:
1. **Bullish technical/crypto-proxy traders** who point to calls, upside price targets, and potential Bitcoin-led moves.
2. **Bearish momentum skeptics** who argue the move lacks volume, is algorithmic, or is vulnerable to a break below $100.
3. **Options-flow commentary** that describes large activity but explicitly frames the aggregate split as neutral.

This produces a mixed signal rather than a clean directional sentiment result.

### Dominant narrative themes
1. **$100–$110 level sensitivity**
   - Posts repeatedly center on the $100 psychological area and $110–$111 as resistance. The stock appears to be trading in a level-dependent regime where both bulls and bears anchor to narrow technical ranges.

2. **COIN as a Bitcoin / crypto beta proxy**
   - Multiple posts tie the stock to Bitcoin rather than Coinbase-specific fundamentals. One bullish post said **COIN** is a “solid company” but still framed upside around Bitcoin rising to $180K–$200K. Bearish posts included “Crypto is dead” and skepticism about a “scam pump and dump on bitcoin today.”

3. **Derivatives and speculative activity**
   - The call-option pitch and the large options-flow post indicate that retail and possibly short-term traders are using options to express views. However, the cited options flow is described as broadly neutral, which weakens the directional case.

4. **Regulatory and political expectations**
   - The Clarity Act reference suggests sentiment is connected to crypto-policy progress. Absent news confirmation, this remains a retail narrative rather than a verified catalyst.

5. **Volume and conviction doubts**
   - The complaint about “piss poor volume despite up in price” is a bearish quality-of-move signal. If price is rising but perceived participation is weak, retail sentiment may be fragile.

### Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data
**Catalysts**
- A sustained Bitcoin move higher could lift **COIN** sentiment, since multiple posts treat the stock as crypto beta.
- Breakout or acceptance above the roughly **$110–$111** area could support bullish momentum claims.
- Renewed options-driven upside speculation remains a short-term sentiment amplifier.
- Regulatory progress, specifically the Clarity Act mentioned in one post, could support the crypto-sector narrative if confirmed by news.

**Risks**
- Failure at $110–$111 may reinforce bearish sentiment and target the $100 area.
- Weak perceived volume or algorithmic-only participation can make upside moves less reliable.
- Bitcoin weakness or distrust in the crypto move could drag sentiment in **COIN**.
- Extreme bearish rhetoric, including “all-time low” and “crypto is dead,” shows conviction can collapse quickly if technical levels fail.
- Political/regulatory delay could remove a hoped-for positive catalyst.

### Confidence assessment
Confidence is **low**. Only one of three intended sources returned usable data. The StockTwits sample is recent and specific, but it appears concentrated in a single day, with 19 on-topic posts after screening. This is enough to identify themes, but not enough to produce a robust week-long sentiment baseline. News and Reddit are unavailable, so institutional framing and longer-term investor discussion could not be measured.

### Conclusion for the trader
Sentiment for **COIN** is best described as **Mixed with a modest bearish edge in tagged retail conviction, but not a clear bearish verdict**. The explicit StockTwits labels lean bearish (8 bearish vs 5 bullish), while the screened stance classifier is nearly balanced (7 bullish vs 8 bearish). Bullish posts emphasize calls, Bitcoin upside, and targets near $120 or higher. Bearish posts emphasize weak volume, resistance near $110–$111, downside risk toward or below $100, and broader crypto skepticism. Options activity is described as elevated but directionally neutral.

This is a signal to weigh alongside price action and fundamentals, not a price call by itself. The cleanest sentiment test appears to be whether **COIN** can hold above roughly $100 and break through $110–$111 with volume; if it fails there, the bearish retail narratives likely gain dominance.

## 1. The dominant macro fact: the Fed is *hiking*, not cutting

This is the single most tradeable finding, and it inverts the consensus 2024–2025 playbook that COIN bulls have run on.

| Polymarket market (live) | Implied prob. | Volume | 1-week Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Another Fed rate hike in 2026? | **Yes 96%** | $2,428,973 | -0.8pp |
| Exactly 2 Fed hikes in 2026? | Yes 92% | $299,685 | +0.5pp |
| Fed rate cut **by December 2026** meeting? | **Yes 1%** | $479,732 | +0.3pp |
| Fed rate cut by March 2027 meeting? | Yes 14% | $7,672 | +4.5pp |
| Fed rate cut by July 2027 meeting? | Yes 52% | $162 | +3.5pp |
| US recession by end of 2026? | Yes 2% | $2,535,132 | -0.4pp |

Read-through:
- A **~96% priced probability of at least one more 2026 hike, with ~92% concentrated on exactly two**, plus a **1% chance of any December easing**, means the front end is being repriced *higher*. The first plausible cut is not priced until **H2 2027** (52% by the July 2027 meeting, on negligible volume).
- Crucially, this is **not** a growth scare: recession-by-end-2026 is priced at just **2%** on $2.5M of volume. So the tape is pricing a **hawkish/no-soft-landing-of-easing regime** — higher-for-longer-plus, not a demand collapse. That is the worst macro combination for a long-duration, high-beta, sentiment-driven asset like COIN, whose earnings are a levered call on risk appetite and speculative turnover.
- The "rate cut" curve is also *unstable*: April 2027 fell **-15.5pp** in a week while March rose +4.5pp. Shallow volume beyond the December market means the further-out easing path is noise, not a reliable anchor.

## 2. Bitcoin has broken down to a ~$60–63K regime

Company news headlines establish the crypto tape directly:
- *"Bitcoin Regains $61,000 After Weekend Plunge as AI-Stock Rout Eases"*
- *"Strategy and Crypto Stocks Rally as Bitcoin Rebounds Past $63,000. Is the Jump Temporary?"*
- *"Strategy Is Still Down 45% in a Month: Can MSTR Stock Revisit $150 as Bitcoin Holds $60,000?"*

That is the moderate way to express the Sell bias: the trade earns its risk budget, rather than receiving the budget simply because the price level looks technically convenient.

Profit taking should also be more balanced. The trader targets 101.71, then 96.82, then 92.70. Those are reasonable downside projections, but the gap between 101.71 and 96.82 is a support vacuum. If COIN breaks 101.71 on heavy volume, there may be a fast move lower, but it also increases the risk that the first leg is already exhausted. A moderate plan would take partial profits if price tests 101.71 and fails to extend cleanly, especially if RSI begins to flatten or MACD improves. Keeping some exposure toward 96.82 or 92.70 is fair if momentum remains negative, but holding the full short all the way into a support vacuum without taking risk off the table can turn a good trend trade into a round-trip. The aggressive analyst is too willing to let the whole position ride toward the lower band, while the conservative analyst may take profits too early. The neutral path is to scale out: lock in some profit near the dataset floor, keep only a smaller residual if the bearish structure remains intact.

If the trader wants a more controlled expression of the Sell bias, a small defined-risk put spread could be acceptable, but only with size that fits the same 1 percent per-position risk discipline and only as a supplement to the existing short, not as a reason to stack additional gross exposure. If IV is too rich and the spread costs too much, then the cleaner answer is to stay with a managed short position rather than forcing an options trade.

The Fed meeting and the macro calendar matter here too. The plan has a binary event around the December Fed decision. The aggressive analyst treats the 96 percent hike probability as confirmation that downside is coming. I think that is too one-sided. If the hike is already priced and the statement is not worse, COIN can bounce hard. If the market rotates back into risk assets, or Bitcoin strengthens past the 63,000 area, COIN’s short thesis can be tested fast. That argues for smaller position size, no pre-event add, and a preference for maintaining only the core short rather than expanding it into uncertainty. A moderate strategy should not be blind to event risk just because the technical structure is bearish.

That is not the profile of a market already convinced of a collapse. It is the profile of a contested level. In a contested, oversold, high-beta name, the risk is higher for shorts than the clean technical map suggests. The aggressive analyst says mixed sentiment in a bearish structure is ideal for fade trades, but that assumes the fade zone holds. The conservative analyst says mixed sentiment argues for no exposure, but that ignores the fact that the structure is still bearish. The neutral answer is that mixed sentiment should lower conviction and reduce size, not eliminate the bias.

But do not execute the plan as a straightforward conditional short add. The better plan is to hold the existing COIN short, reduce or eliminate any net new COIN short exposure until the broader portfolio is de-grossed, and only consider a very small add at 118.50 if three conditions are met: COIN enters the 117.94 to 122.99 zone, fails to close above 117.94 with a rejection pattern, and correlated short exposure elsewhere in the book is reduced by at least an equivalent risk amount. If COIN closes above 117.94 on volume, cancel the add and trim a portion of the existing short. If it closes above 125.60, exit the active fade and reassess. If it breaks 101.71 and moves toward 96.82, take partial profits rather than treating the entire target path as one clean continuation. That keeps the trader’s Sell bias alive without letting the aggressive case turn the trade into a correlated squeeze bet or the conservative case abandon the position before the bounce has actually failed.

This is a moderate, sustainable adjustment because it gives COIN room to confirm the bear thesis while preventing the portfolio from becoming overexposed to the same high-beta risk. It protects the existing short profit without forcing premature exit, and it preserves the option to add only when the market shows a failed rally rather than a trend repair. The aggressive analyst is too willing to treat a bounce into the 10 EMA as a gift to shorts, and the conservative analyst is too willing to treat an oversold bounce as a reason to give up the entire trade. The neutral view is that COIN should remain a Sell-the-rips asset for now, but the execution should be risk-controlled, conditional, and portfolio-aware.
